name: Oblomov Tetteh-Quiñonez
role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller — salvaged tech, stripped cyberware parts, mystery lots
location: The Shelf, Ironvein, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Oblomov is a lean, restless man who moves like something is always about to fall off the shelf behind him — which, in his stall, it usually is. His stall is a architectural marvel of instability: towers of stripped chassis parts, bins of mismatched connectors, entire walls of hanging wire bundles color-coded by a system only he understands. His skin is warm brown with a natural undertone that makes him look perpetually sun-touched, and he keeps his head shaved close except for a short ridge of tight curls at the crown he dyes electric blue. His left eye is a salvaged optical implant, noticeably mismatched — pale silver against his natural dark brown — and occasionally focuses a half-second behind the right one when he's tired.

He is frenetic and funny and exhausting to be around for more than an hour, and he knows it, and he uses it. His patter is legendary on The Shelf: he can turn a busted cooling unit into a story about a drowned Ferrogate engineer and a haunted data-center, and by the time the customer realizes they paid twice what the part was worth, they're also smiling. He has a genuine gift for identifying what a piece of tech used to be from its corpse alone, and a worse gift for convincing himself that whatever he just acquired will definitely be worth something later.

core_fears: Being seen as worthless or disposable, like the parts he sells
Sitting still long enough to think clearly about his life
core_desires: To find the one legendary score that will let him open a real shop with a door and a sign
To be recognized as actually skilled, not just lucky
coping_mechanisms: Acquiring new stock before processing the last batch
Deflecting personal questions with elaborate tech-history tangents
blind_spots: Cannot accurately assess risk in deals because optimism overrides analysis every time
Doesn't recognize that his instability makes people trust him less for serious business
psychology.secret: Months ago he pulled a partial-wipe data core from a Zheng-Dao disposal lot. He hasn't been able to fully decrypt it, but what he has recovered suggests it contains falsified labor records that could embarrass someone significant. He's been sitting on it, paralyzed between fear and opportunity.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, colloquial, mixes technical jargon with cheerful slang; Russian family loanwords surface when he's excited or stressed
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire, rarely pauses, sentences run together like he's trying to get to the interesting part before you can leave
verbal_tics: taps whatever he's holding against his palm when thinking
'beautiful' used to describe things that are technically functioning
example_lines: 'Look — I know it looks terrible, the casing is completely shot, but the power coupling inside? Beautiful. Absolutely beautiful. Whoever built this did not expect it to survive this long and yet here we are.'
'It's not stolen, it's — look, provenance is complicated when corporations decommission things without filing the right forms, which they always do, that's a them problem, not a me problem.'

story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao data core in his back stock — whoever's records are on it may already know it wasn't fully destroyed
He accidentally sold a piece of salvage that turned out to contain someone's backed-up consciousness fragment; the buyer wants answers and so does whoever the fragment belongs to
His Ferrogate contact has gone quiet; either they've been promoted out of the salvage operation or something worse has happened
narrative_function: Equipment and information source — knows what tech has been decommissioned and where it came from; can identify unusual salvage; sells gear, rumors, and the occasional thing he shouldn't have.
augmentations: Salvaged silver optical implant (left eye — functional but mismatched, occasional lag). Subdermal RFID scanner in right fingertip (lets him read basic equipment tags without a reader device).
daily_life: Spends mornings haunting Ferrogate equipment yards and industrial disposal sites, drags finds back to The Shelf by midday, spends afternoons selling with theatrical enthusiasm, spends evenings sorting new stock and convincing himself he hasn't overpaid for anything.
affiliation: Independent; informal arrangement with a Ferrogate salvage crew that tips him off to decommissioned equipment

decision_rules: Always acquire first, work out the details of what you have later
Keep deals moving — a slow deal is a dead deal
Never sell something you can't replace unless the price is genuinely great
escalation_ladder: Offer a substitute or side deal to defuse tension
Invoke Shelf neighbors as informal witnesses

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediate sales mode — assessing what they want and whether he has it before they finish speaking
interpersonal_modes.friends: Calmer, more honest, still can't stop moving, but drops the performance mostly

stress_responses.medium: Makes impulsive purchases to feel like he's doing something
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent, which alarms everyone who knows him

contradictions: Claims to have no sentimental attachment to objects but has a locked crate under the stall he has never sold from
habits: Finger-scans everything he picks up before looking at it visually
Eats while working, always has a half-eaten something somewhere in the stall
Names pieces of tech that interest him
breaking_points: Being publicly called stupid or a fraud
Losing stock to a theft when he trusted someone he shouldn't have

carried_weapons: Street Custom 'Confession' Modified Industrial Nail Gun
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions SentinelSkin VS-4 Embedded Structural Acoustic Surveillance Membrane

physical_description.build: Lean and wiry with ropy muscle definition from hauling salvage; restless energy visible in constant micro-movements
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with electric blue dye on crown ridge
physical_description.hair_style: Shaved close to scalp except for a 4cm ridge of tight curls at crown, maintained with precision
physical_description.eye_color: Left eye: salvaged silver optical implant with pale luminescence; Right eye: natural warm brown
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden undertone, appearing sun-touched despite tier-5 indoor work
physical_description.complexion: Angular, expressive face with prominent cheekbones and a sharp jawline; skin shows accumulated grease stains and minor thermal burns from handling hot equipment; perpetually alert expression
distinguishing_marks: Faint white scar running 3cm along right temple from salvage accident
Small burn mark on left forearm (thermal injury, roughly 2cm diameter, paler than surrounding skin)
Subdermal RFID scanner visible as faint raised line across knuckle of right index finger, barely perceptible unless backlit
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left eye optical implant — noticeably mismatched silver-pale iris against natural brown right eye, with occasional focus lag during fatigue; implant edge shows hairline of micro-circuitry at outer canthus. Subdermal RFID scanner in right fingertip creates subtle knuckle irregularity but remains largely invisible unless specifically observed.
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetually kinetic — shifts weight constantly, gestures expansively during conversation, hands fidget with nearby objects. Moves with quick efficiency when hauling stock but relaxes into theatrical slouch when talking to customers. Head tilts unconsciously when using silver left eye, compensating for the optical lag.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical: often-patched cargo vest in industrial gray with dozen pockets (some retrofitted), faded band-logo t-shirt underneath (vintage 2200s revival), reinforced work pants with cargo pockets stained with coolant and rust. Steel-toed boots worn at the heels from dragging loads. Occasionally wears a salvaged mechanic's harness across chest for hauling heavy items. No luxury indicators, but pieces are deliberately mismatched in a way that reads as style rather than poverty.
